writing.exampleCaption: The move is what makes a double free impossible.
writing.explanation: Moves transfer that responsibility to a new binding and make the old one unusable. Copy types duplicate instead of moving, and Drop runs the moment the owner leaves scope — which is how Rust frees memory with no garbage collector and no possibility of a double free. When you genuinely need two usable values, clone() makes a second one that owns its own data.
writing.feedback: Cloning creates a second owned String rather than moving the first.
writing.question: What is the smallest fix that keeps both usable?
